stem: Why should a healthcare workplace-violence prevention program encourage reporting of threats, aggressive behavior, and violent incidents even when no physical injury occurs?

options.A: Because verbal threats should be excluded from documentation so the facility's workplace-safety statistics are not affected.
options.B: Because only incidents causing a recordable physical injury provide useful information for a workplace-violence prevention program.
options.C: Because reports and near-miss records help identify patterns and hazards, support investigation and risk assessment, and guide prevention and program improvement.
options.D: Because incident records are unrelated to prevention; workplace-violence programs depend only on the number of security staff assigned.

rationale: OSHA's hospital workplace-violence eTool encourages prompt reporting of all violent incidents and describes recordkeeping and program evaluation as core prevention-program components. OSHA specifically identifies near-miss reports of verbal attacks or aggressive behavior and explains that records can reveal trends and patterns, evaluate hazard controls, identify training needs, and support solutions. C is therefore correct. A, B, and D would remove information OSHA identifies as important to prevention.
educational_objective: Recognize reporting and recordkeeping of threats, aggressive behavior, close calls, and violent incidents as tools for workplace-hazard detection, trend analysis, and violence-prevention improvement.
source_organization: U.S. Department of Labor, Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA)
source_document_title: Hospitals eTool — Hospital-wide Hazards — Workplace Violence
source_locator: Workplace violence prevention program — prompt reporting and recordkeeping; Program Evaluation and Recordkeeping — Recordkeeping and Elements of program evaluation; Violence Incident Report Form — reportable incident includes threatening remarks or overt violence
source_claim_supported: OSHA encourages prompt reporting of violent incidents, threats and close calls; recordkeeping helps identify trends, assess hazards and controls, and improve workplace-violence prevention programs.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
blueprint_locator: Printed p.8, Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — Promote staff and workplace safety; Protect clients and healthcare personnel from environmental hazards; Follow safety procedures
blueprint_topic: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — workplace-violence reporting and prevention

source_original.stem: Why should a healthcare workplace-violence program encourage reporting of threats and incidents even when no physical injury occurs?

options.A: Verbal threats should not be documented because reporting them can distort workplace safety statistics
options.B: Only injuries requiring medical treatment provide useful information for violence-prevention programs
options.C: Reporting supports pattern detection, risk assessment, investigation, and prevention of future escalation
options.D: Incident records are unrelated to prevention because violence programs rely only on security staffing

source_original.rationale: OSHA guidance encourages prompt reporting and recordkeeping of violent incidents, including threats. Reports help organizations assess hazards, investigate events, measure progress, and refine prevention strategies.
source_original.source_detail: Written program elements: prompt reporting of all violent incidents, recordkeeping, hazard assessment, and program evaluation; accessed 2026-08-14.

correction_summary: Corrected the blueprint from Management of Care to Safety and Infection Prevention and Control because the construct is staff/workplace safety; expanded the stem to OSHA's threats/aggressive-behavior/incident scope, tied the rationale to exact recordkeeping/program-evaluation sections, and reduced difficulty from hard to easy.

audit_findings.source_authority: Current OSHA hospital eTool; NCSBN 2026 Test Plan
audit_findings.currentness: OSHA eTool current at 2026-08-16 and links current recordkeeping requirements/resources.
audit_findings.claim_audit: OSHA directly supports reporting all violent incidents, recording near misses/verbal attacks/aggressive behavior, and using records to identify patterns, hazards, control effectiveness and training needs.

distractor_audit.A: Contradicts OSHA's inclusion of threats and verbal/aggressive incidents.
distractor_audit.B: Contradicts OSHA's near-miss and non-injury incident recordkeeping guidance.
distractor_audit.D: Contradicts OSHA's multidimensional prevention program and program-evaluation requirements.

audit_findings.ambiguity_second_answer: Only C states the prevention value OSHA assigns to reporting and records.
audit_findings.cueing: All options address why to report; no second legitimate reporting purpose competes with C.
audit_findings.blueprint: Corrected to Safety and Infection Prevention and Control, printed p.8, because NCSBN explicitly includes staff/workplace safety.
audit_findings.independent_second_pass: Re-read OSHA prompt-reporting, recordkeeping, near-miss and evaluation sections, challenged category placement and whether only OSHA-recordable injuries count, and confirmed C remained uniquely correct.
